assessment: The source packet is a single LaTeX file (main_S.tex) containing the full text of the paper 'Compatible Instability: Gauge Constraints of Elasticity Inherited by Electronic Nematic Criticality' by W. Joe Meese and Rafael M. Fernandes. The paper develops a phenomenological theory of nemato-elasticity in an isotropic elastic medium, introducing a helical basis for the nematic order parameter and strain. The key quantitative result is the effective nematic free energy density (Eq. 6, line 137), which shows that only two of the five helical nematic components (Phi_2 and Phi_3) are critical, while the other three (Phi_1, Phi_4, Phi_5) acquire a gap proportional to lambda_0^2/mu. The paper also derives the nemato-plastic free energy (Eq. 8, line 156) and the effective conjugate nematic field (Eq. 9, line 163). The extraction focuses on the effective nematic free energy density as the central quantitative cluster, with the control being the momentum magnitude q and the readout being the effective free energy density f_eff. The two regimes are the critical directions (where Phi_1=Phi_4=Phi_5=0) and the gapped directions (where Phi_1, Phi_4, or Phi_5 are nonzero). The paper does not report numerical values for the parameters lambda_0, mu, lambda, or r, so the parameters are recorded with symbolic values (set to 1 as placeholders, with uncertainty 'source_unspecified' and role 'symbolic'). The case is authoring-ready because there is a numeric control (q), a numeric readout (f_eff), a quantitative mechanism (the free energy equation), and an objective source-grounded response within an explicit domain (q>0).

paper_scope: The paper develops a phenomenological theory of nemato-elasticity in an isotropic elastic medium, showing that elastic compatibility relations split the five helical nematic order parameters into two critical (Phi_2, Phi_3) and three gapped (Phi_1, Phi_4, Phi_5) modes. It derives the effective nematic free energy density and the nemato-plastic free energy, and discusses the implications for direction-selective criticality and disorder effects.
